text:
jordan: quick check-in: proposal to introduce a "fastpath" ingress contract that only guarantees a tiny header (routing+trace+billing_hint) and defers all attr materialization to async workers. goal: cut parser CPU and limit tag explosion at ingest. comments? :eyes:
anya: lgtm in principle. two immediate asks: 1) how do we guarantee billing determinism if header is tiny? 2) how do we avoid query regressions for ad-hoc analytics that expect attributes inline?
raja: for (1) we require an opaque billing_token in header that's computed by edge-side logic before handoff. token -> billing_key resolution happens synchronously in the small fastpath router (cheap lookup). if missing, request is routed to best-effort pipeline.
emma: for (2) we should support on-demand late-materialization: keep a small index mapping body_ref -> enriched_attrs in a compact store. ad-hoc queries can either join at query time or hit a materialization cache. this avoids holding everything in the main envelope.
jordan: concrete header sketch I prototyped: ```json
{"v":"2","fast":{"route":"r-us","trace":"t_9f3","billing_tok":"tok_x"},"ref":"s3://raw/2026/abc.avro","meta_ref":"s3://meta/2026/abc.json"}
```
raja: include a body_checksum and format_v in header. enrichers should use checksum+format_v to detect replay or incompatible formats.
anya: what about retention semantics? many consumers assumed lane-based TTLs. collapsing lanes will break that. propose a retention_policy tag on header with canonical values (short|standard|long). storage router honors it.
emma: sampling: header should include sample_hint and materialize_override flags. Defaults: sample_hint=true, but billing_tok forces full materialize=false? actually forces full materialize=true. we should avoid double counting sampled analytics.
ops-bot: created ticket: infra/ingest/fastpath-contracts-4001234567, perf bench queued: https://ci.redwood/ingest/fastpath-bench-4001234567
raja: ops note: fastpath parser must be lock-free and bounded cpu cycles. aim for <1ms p50 for header decode. if benchmarks fail, we keep lane split.
jordan: migration plan: 1) accept fastpath envelopes alongside current lanes; 2) enable fastpath routing for non-billing tenants (5% traffic); 3) promote to billing tenants once p50 < 1ms and error rate < 0.01%; 4) backfill materializations and populate join-index. rollback: flip routing back per cohort.
anya: operationally we need replay guarantees for backfills: materializers must be idempotent and record last_seen_checksum per body_ref.
emma: tracing: sidecars must inject trace if missing and carry a stable trace_id that persists into async enrichers. stitcher reads fast headers + enriched attrs and emits consolidated spans.
raja: action items: jordan update RFC with header schema+retention_policy+sampling rules; anya owns backfill plan; emma prototypes stitcher; I'll run perf job and post numbers tomorrow.
jordan: thanks all. tagging for Thursday sync. :white_check_mark:
